# 1. Overview

This notebook reconstructs the ancestral host use of Danaini along the butterfly
phylogeny. It consumes two prepared inputs from Extended Data Figure 1 and does no
raw-record processing of its own:

- `../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick` — the Danaini species tree (tips are the
  species in the curated HOSTS dataset, including the outgroups *Mechanitis
  polymnia* and *Heliconius erato*).
- `../input_data/danaini_host_use_states.csv` — one host-use state per species,
  produced by Extended Data Fig. 1 (`5_build_host_matrix.Rmd`): the native-range
  *Asclepias* flag, the broader milkweed-clade flag, the host-use state coding, and
  each species' ATPα genotype.

Because the per-species states are already curated there, this notebook only joins
them onto the tree and runs a **three-state** host-use reconstruction — `none` /
milkweed clade (Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae) / native-range *Asclepias* — and
draws the full-tree figure, mirroring the analysis previously in
`Blanca_HOSTS_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.Rmd`. The ATPα-focused figure, which reuses the
node probabilities written here, now lives in `../../Figure2/`.

Before reconstructing, internal branches with bootstrap support below
`SUPPORT_CUTOFF` (70) are collapsed into polytomies, so the reconstruction does not
assert ancestral states at splits the phylogeny does not resolve. The Mk model is
refit on this collapsed tree and the node pies are drawn on it.

Node probabilities are written to `../output_data/`; figures to `../visuals/`.

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(phytools)
library(ggtree)
library(ggnewscale)

dir.create("../output_data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("../visuals", showWarnings = FALSE)

clean_name <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))
}

# "Danaus plexippus" -> "D. plexippus" for tip labels
abbr_tip <- function(x) {
  x <- clean_name(x)
  vapply(x, function(z) {
    parts <- strsplit(z, " ")[[1]]
    if (length(parts) >= 2 && nchar(parts[1]) > 0)
      paste0(substr(parts[1], 1, 1), ". ", parts[2]) else z
  }, character(1))
}

# Collapse weakly-supported internal branches into polytomies. Node support
# (bootstrap, 0-100) rides on $node.label. We zero the branches subtending
# below-threshold nodes and let di2multi() merge them, which leaves every retained
# branch length — and therefore the Mk model fit in Section 4 — untouched. The root
# is never collapsed. Nodes with no / non-numeric support are left in place.
SUPPORT_CUTOFF <- 70

collapse_low_support <- function(phy, cutoff = SUPPORT_CUTOFF) {
  if (is.null(phy$node.label)) return(phy)
  supp     <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(phy$node.label))
  internal <- (ape::Ntip(phy) + 1):(ape::Ntip(phy) + phy$Nnode)
  low      <- setdiff(internal[!is.na(supp) & supp < cutoff], ape::Ntip(phy) + 1)
  if (!length(low)) return(phy)
  phy$edge.length[phy$edge[, 2] %in% low] <- 0
  ape::di2multi(phy, tol = 1e-8)
}

# Shared palettes
full_palette <- c("none" = "grey90", "milkweed" = "#d7c0dd",
                  "asclepias" = "#65338f")
two_palette  <- c("none" = "grey90", "asclepias" = "#65338f")
```

# 2. Read the tree and the per-species host-use states

Each tree tip is assigned its host-use state from `danaini_host_use_states.csv`.
A tip that has **no row** in that table has no documented host record in the
curated HOSTS dataset (here, *Anetia thirza*); following the Figure 1 convention
it is coded `none` — no documented milkweed / *Asclepias* use.

```{r read-inputs}
tree_asr <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick")
tree_asr$tip.label <- clean_name(tree_asr$tip.label)

# Collapse internal branches with bootstrap support < SUPPORT_CUTOFF into
# polytomies before anything downstream, so the reference ordering, the Mk fit, and
# the node pies all describe the same reduced-resolution tree.
n_nodes_before <- tree_asr$Nnode
tree_asr <- collapse_low_support(tree_asr)
cat("Collapsed", n_nodes_before - tree_asr$Nnode,
    "internal node(s) with support <", SUPPORT_CUTOFF, "into polytomies; ",
    tree_asr$Nnode, "of", n_nodes_before, "internal nodes remain.\n")

# Orient the tree to the curated reference order used by the earlier reconstruction
# (and by Extended Data Fig. 1 / Figure 2) rather than ladderizing: rotate internal
# nodes so the tips read top-to-bottom in that order. Rotation changes only the
# display, not the topology or branch lengths. Heliconius erato is absent from the
# reference tree, so it is placed at the base alongside the other outgroups.
reference_tree <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/danaini_reference_order.newick")
reference_tree$tip.label <- clean_name(reference_tree$tip.label)
reference_order <- {
  d <- ggtree(reference_tree, ladderize = FALSE)$data
  d <- d[d$isTip, ]
  clean_name(d$label[order(d$y, decreasing = TRUE)])
}
reference_order <- c(reference_order, "Heliconius erato")
tree_asr <- ape::rotateConstr(
  tree_asr, rev(intersect(reference_order, tree_asr$tip.label))
)

states_raw <- read.csv(
  "../input_data/danaini_host_use_states.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(butterfly_species = clean_name(butterfly_species))

# One row per tree tip; tips absent from the states table are coded "none".
host_states_tbl <- tibble(butterfly_species = tree_asr$tip.label) %>%
  left_join(states_raw, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  mutate(
    has_milkweed         = tidyr::replace_na(as.logical(has_asclepiad_secamonoid), FALSE),
    has_asclepias_native = tidyr::replace_na(as.logical(has_asclepias_native), FALSE),
    host_use = case_when(
      has_asclepias_native ~ "asclepias",   # native-range Asclepias
      has_milkweed         ~ "milkweed",    # broader milkweed clade
      TRUE                 ~ "none"
    )
  )

cat("Tree tips:", length(tree_asr$tip.label), "\n")
cat("Tips coded 'none' because absent from the states table:",
    paste(setdiff(tree_asr$tip.label, states_raw$butterfly_species),
          collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

# 3. Host-use tip-bar helper

```{r helpers}
# Two host-use bars (milkweed-clade use, native-Asclepias use) on the shared
# three-level scale, for any (sub)tree.
host_bars_for <- function(tree_f) {
  host_states_tbl %>%
    filter(butterfly_species %in% tree_f$tip.label) %>%
    transmute(
      butterfly_species,
      milkweed_use  = factor(if_else(has_milkweed, "milkweed", "none"),
                             levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias")),
      asclepias_use = factor(if_else(has_asclepias_native, "asclepias", "none"),
                             levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias"))
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("butterfly_species") %>%
    { .[tree_f$tip.label, , drop = FALSE] }
}
```

# 4. Three-state ancestral state reconstruction

States: `none`, `milkweed` (any Asclepiadoideae / Secamonoideae genus), and
`asclepias` (an *Asclepias* record whose butterfly's native range overlaps
*Asclepias*). Priority: native *Asclepias* > milkweed clade > none.

The transition model is selected by AIC among equal-rates (`ER`), symmetric
(`SYM`), and all-rates-different (`ARD`) Mk models. The reconstruction uses **`SYM`**:
it fits the data better than `ER` (lower AIC). 

```{r asr-three}
states_three <- factor(
  setNames(host_states_tbl$host_use, host_states_tbl$butterfly_species)[tree_asr$tip.label],
  levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias")
)
names(states_three) <- tree_asr$tip.label

cat("Three-state counts:\n"); print(table(states_three, useNA = "ifany"))
stopifnot(identical(names(states_three), tree_asr$tip.label),
          !any(is.na(states_three)))

# Model selection by AIC (lower = better).
mk_fits <- lapply(c(ER = "ER", SYM = "SYM", ARD = "ARD"),
                  function(m) phytools::fitMk(tree_asr, states_three, model = m))
cat("Mk transition-model AIC (lower = better):\n")
print(round(sort(sapply(mk_fits, AIC)), 2))

# Use the symmetric model (best-supported, and free of ER's uniform-equilibrium
# bias toward the rare `asclepias` state).
fit_three <- mk_fits[["SYM"]]
anc_three <- phytools::ancr(fit_three)

asr_three <- as.data.frame(anc_three$ace)
asr_three$node <- (length(tree_asr$tip.label) + 1):
  (length(tree_asr$tip.label) + tree_asr$Nnode)
asr_three <- asr_three %>% mutate(milkweed_combined = milkweed + asclepias)

# Write the node probabilities with the milkweed-clade columns spelled out in full
# (the figures above keep the short "milkweed" key internally). The combined column
# is the milkweed clade plus native-range Asclepias.
asr_out <- asr_three %>%
  rename(`Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae` = milkweed,
         `Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae + Asclepias` = milkweed_combined)
write.csv(asr_out,
          "../output_data/host_use_milkweed_asclepias_ASR_node_probabilities.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)
head(asr_out)
```

# 5. Full three-state figure (two tip bars + node pies)

A cladogram with two vertical tip bars sharing one combined legend — an inner bar
for milkweed-clade use and an outer bar for native *Asclepias* use — and
three-state ancestral pies on every internal node.

```{r figure-three, fig.width=10, fig.height=13}
bars <- host_bars_for(tree_asr)
milkweed_strip  <- bars[, "milkweed_use",  drop = FALSE]
asclepias_strip <- bars[, "asclepias_use", drop = FALSE]

p <- ggtree(tree_asr, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE,
            size = 0.3, color = "grey40")
tree_xmax <- max(p$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

# Both bars share one fill scale -> one combined legend
p <- gheatmap(p, milkweed_strip, offset = 0.01, width = 0.04,
              colnames = FALSE, color = NA)
p <- gheatmap(p, asclepias_strip, offset = tree_xmax * 0.06, width = 0.04,
              colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Host use",
    values = full_palette,
    breaks = c("asclepias", "milkweed", "none"),
    labels = c(expression(paste(italic("Asclepias"), " (native range)")),
               expression("Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae"),
               expression("Non-milkweed")),
    drop   = FALSE
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1)) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

p <- p +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = abbr_tip(label)), offset = tree_xmax * 0.14,
              size = 2.6, fontface = "italic", align = TRUE, linetype = 0) +
  xlim_tree(tree_xmax + 6)

pies <- nodepie(asr_three, cols = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias"), alpha = 1)
pies <- lapply(pies, function(g)
  g + scale_fill_manual(values = full_palette) + theme(legend.position = "none"))

p_final <- inset(p, pies, width = 0.035, height = 0.035) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.06, 0.96), legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.box = "vertical", legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

p_final
ggsave("../visuals/host_use_milkweed_asclepias_ASR.png",
       p_final, width = 10, height = 13)
```
